points: In the second year of the reign of Darius, Aggeus and Zacharias the son of Addo, the prophets, prophesied unto the Jews in Jewry and Jerusalem in the name of the Lord God of Israel.

note.label: 1 Esdras 6: The Letter to Darius and the Record Found at Ecbatane

points: Then stood up Zorobabel the son of Salathiel, and Jesus the son of Josedec, and began to build the house of the Lord at Jerusalem, the prophets of the Lord being with them, and helping them.

note.label: 1 Esdras 6: The Letter to Darius and the Record Found at Ecbatane

points: Sisinnes the governor of Syria and Phenice, with his companions, came and asked, By whose appointment do ye build this house?

note.label: 1 Esdras 6: The Letter to Darius and the Record Found at Ecbatane

points: Nevertheless the elders of the Jews obtained favour, because the Lord had visited the captivity; and they were not hindered from building, until such time as signification was given unto Darius concerning them, and an answer received.

note.label: 1 Esdras 6: The Letter to Darius and the Record Found at Ecbatane

points: The letter to Darius reported that the ancients of the Jews were building an house unto the Lord, great and new, of hewn and costly stones, and the timber already laid upon the walls, and that the work went on prosperously in their hands.

note.label: 1 Esdras 6: The Letter to Darius and the Record Found at Ecbatane

points: The elders answered, We are the servants of the Lord that made heaven and earth; and as for this house, it was builded many years ago by a king of Israel great and strong, and was finished.

note.label: 1 Esdras 6: The Letter to Darius and the Record Found at Ecbatane

points: When our fathers provoked God unto wrath, and sinned against the Lord of Israel which is in heaven, he gave them over into the power of Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon, who pulled down the house, and burned it, and carried away the people captives unto Babylon.

note.label: 1 Esdras 6: The Letter to Darius and the Record Found at Ecbatane

points: In the first year that Cyrus reigned over the country of Babylon, king Cyrus wrote to build up this house, and delivered the holy vessels again, with commandment that they should be set in the temple at Jerusalem.

note.label: 1 Esdras 6: The Letter to Darius and the Record Found at Ecbatane

points: Now therefore, if it seem good unto the king, let search be made among the records of king Cyrus.

note.label: 1 Esdras 6: The Letter to Darius and the Record Found at Ecbatane

points: Darius commanded to seek among the records at Babylon; and at Ecbatane the palace, which is in the country of Media, there was found a roll wherein these things were recorded.

note.label: 1 Esdras 6: The Letter to Darius and the Record Found at Ecbatane

points: In the first year of the reign of Cyrus, king Cyrus commanded that the house of the Lord at Jerusalem should be built again, where they do sacrifice with continual fire, and that the expenses thereof be given out of the king's house, and the holy vessels restored.

note.label: 1 Esdras 6: The Letter to Darius and the Record Found at Ecbatane

points: Darius commanded that Sisinnes and his companions should not meddle with the place, but suffer Zorobabel the servant of the Lord, and governor of Judea, and the elders of the Jews, to build the house of the Lord in that place.

note.label: 1 Esdras 6: The Letter to Darius and the Record Found at Ecbatane

points: Out of the tribute of Celosyria and Phenice a portion was to be carefully given for the sacrifices of the Lord continually every year, that offerings may be made unto the most high God for the king and for his children.

note.label: 1 Esdras 6: The Letter to Darius and the Record Found at Ecbatane

points: The Lord, whose name is there called upon, utterly destroy every king and nation that stretcheth out his hand to hinder or endamage that house of the Lord in Jerusalem.
